concept.name: FX spot
concept.definition: A transaction for the exchange of two currencies at a rate agreed on the trade date for settlement on the standard spot value date, normally two business days later (T+2). Spot is one of the core OTC FX instrument categories in the BIS Triennial Survey and accounted for 28% of the $7.5 trillion average daily global FX turnover in April 2022.
concept.intuition: A spot FX deal is 'buy currency now at today's rate', with the actual exchange of funds settling a couple of business days later.
concept.mechanics: Counterparties agree a rate and amounts on the trade date; the two currency legs are delivered on the spot value date (T+2 for most major pairs, T+1 for some such as USD/CAD). Spot transactions settle delivery-versus-payment through systems like CLS for eligible currencies and form the price base from which forwards and swaps are derived.
concept.failure_modes: Spot quotes embed the T+2 settlement convention, so around holidays the actual value date shifts; settlement (Herstatt) risk exists for non-CLS-settled currencies, and spot prices can gap over weekends when the OTC market is closed.
concept.misconceptions: 'Spot' does not mean immediate same-day settlement — the standard is T+2 — and spot FX is overwhelmingly an OTC interbank/dealer market, not an exchange-traded one.
concept.example: On Monday a corporate treasurer buys EUR 1 million against USD at 1.0850; the euros and dollars are exchanged on Wednesday, the T+2 spot value date.

citations.source: BIS — OTC foreign exchange turnover in April 2022 (Triennial Central Bank Survey)
